headline_summary: Applied Optoelectronics is a 28-year-old founder-led vertically-integrated optical components and transceivers maker that, in FY2025, doubled revenue to $455.7M on the back of a simultaneous CATV cyclical recovery and an AI-datacenter 800G ramp. Customer concentration is severe (Digicomm + Microsoft = 81.9% of FY25), and a $324M+ near-term order book announced March-April 2026 from one hyperscale customer (widely understood to be Amazon, following the March 2025 warrant) marks an inflection toward 1.6T-generation product economics.
founder_ceo: Dr. Chih-Hsiang "Thompson" Lin (Chairman, President, CEO since inception)
structural_thesis_in_one_paragraph: AAOI is the rare US-listed optical components company that operates with full vertical integration from InP wafer fabrication through transceiver assembly, and it has come through a 2018-2023 trough that wiped out roughly $500M of accumulated equity to reach the AI-datacenter ramp with both its vertical stack and its Texas/Taiwan/China manufacturing footprint intact. The investment question is whether the FY2025 result — 82.8% revenue growth, 30% gross margin, narrowed net loss — represents the beginning of a multi-year operating leverage cycle that finally turns the accumulated deficit into book equity, or a cyclical peak compounded by extreme customer concentration that will mean-revert as Microsoft's share normalises and Digicomm's CATV channel matures. The Amazon warrant and the >$324M near-term 1.6T-inclusive order book argue for the first interpretation; the $493.1M accumulated deficit and the 81.9% two-customer concentration argue for caution about the second.
